newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank Leumi rejects offer for Africa Israel - sources.
newsitem.headline: Bank Leumi rejects offer for Africa Israel - sources.

text.p: Entrepreneurs Motti Zisser and Eitan Wertheimer have offered to purchase from Bank Leumi all of its 52 percent stake in Africa Israel Investments but the Bank has refused the offer, banking sources said.
The offer was made at a meeting on Tuesday between Zisser and Wertheimer and Bank Leumi senior officials.

Press reports said that the two bought nine percent of Africa shares outside the bourse on Tuesday, at a price of 110 million shekels, raising their holdings in the company to nearly 16 percent. Zisser and Wertheimer already held a 6.82 percent stake in Africa Israel.
Zisser and Wertheimer were unavailable for comment and Bank Leumi declined to comment.

According to press reports Zisser and Wertheimer last week withdrew their bid from the tender for Africa Israel after Bank Leumi decided to spin off Africa's insurance subsidiary, Migdal, from the company before the sale of Africa. Italian insurer Generali has offered to purchase Migdal.
Press reports said that Zisser and Wertheimer are looking to raise their stake in the company to 25 percent in order to block the spin-off of Migdal from Africa Israel.

Shares in Africa Israel Investments soared the maximum 10 percent on Tuesday on rumours that an investor was looking to purchase shares in the company to the value of $5 million at 15 percent above the market price.

Wertheimer is president of Iscar Ltd, a maker of metal-cutting tools, which he jointly owns with his father Stef. Zisser, president of Control Centres, is a real estate entrepreneur. - Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-22-11
